assumptions.statement: Founders value checked definitions (the term engine and Lean) enough that it should be marketed, not only used inside.
assumptions.test: Show 5 target founders the docket with and without term-checked labels; ask them to explain a decision record back.
assumptions.pass: 3 of 5 name the checked terms unprompted as a reason to trust the record

assumptions.statement: The term engine is needed at all: without it, definition drift would cause wrong agent writes that tests would not catch.
assumptions.test: Count, over one month of dogfooding, writes the term engine refused that schema checks alone would have let through.
assumptions.pass: At least one refused write a person agrees was wrong

assumptions.statement: Early users will run agents on their own AI subscription (Claude Code, MCP) rather than buy credits from us.
assumptions.test: Of the first 10 sign-ups, record which door they use and whether they ask for hosted agents.
assumptions.pass: 7 of 10 run through their own subscription

assumptions.statement: Mentura users without an AI subscription will pay a monthly plan that includes model credits.
assumptions.test: Offer a priced plan with included credits to 10 Main Street operators.

assumptions.statement: Non-technical small business owners (e.g. online fitness coaching) will run their business's decisions in Mentura weekly.
assumptions.test: Onboard 5 such owners by hand; observe 4 weeks.
assumptions.pass: 3 of 5 decide at least one decision a week for 4 weeks

assumptions.statement: AI-native solo founders adopt the plugin and keep using it after the first week.
assumptions.test: Track plugin installs from Torian's network; ask at day 7 and day 30.

assumptions.statement: Venture studios will pay to run several ventures under one method.
A done-with-you venture setup service is a faster first revenue than software.
assumptions.test: Offer the setup service to 5 early accounts at a stated price.

assumptions.statement: Founders will buy or share templates, kits and playbooks built on Naive.
assumptions.test: Publish 3 free templates; measure installs and requests for more.

assumptions.statement: Pooled, anonymised benchmarks from run ventures become a product investors want.
assumptions.test: Not before data terms exist and a minimum group size is decided; then ask 5 investors.
assumptions.pass: TBD by Torian; blocked until data terms exist

assumptions.statement: Licensing observed-venture profiles outward is a viable line (the PitchBook model).
assumptions.test: Legal review first: it would likely make Naive a registered data broker in California.
assumptions.pass: Default: do not pursue unless counsel and Torian approve

assumptions.statement: Others will build on Naive (kits, connectors, frameworks), the Platform phase gate.
assumptions.test: Publish the kit and connector contract; count outside contributions.

assumptions.statement: Agents that buy and sell for a venture (agent payment protocols) become a capability small businesses expect within the planning horizon.
assumptions.test: Watch protocol adoption (ACP, AP2, MPP) and ask early accounts.

assumptions.statement: Small business programs and partners (studios, accelerators, local business centres) are a cheaper channel than direct.
assumptions.test: Approach 2 partners with a pilot cohort.

assumptions.statement: A phase belongs to each premise or function, not only to the whole venture, because real ventures loop back.
assumptions.test: Dogfood venture:naive for a month and log every time a single venture phase was wrong for part of it.
assumptions.pass: 3+ logged mismatches means per-premise phases are needed

assumptions.statement: A site generated from the venture's own records, with a working sign-up, persuades partners more than a deck.
assumptions.test: Show the generated site and sign-up to Jon and Oleena and the first accounts; record their questions.
assumptions.pass: They sign up or ask to bring someone
